model_fitness.best_available_model: Symptomatic heterozygous female Mecp2+/- mice (and Mecp2-/y males for mechanism) studied with simultaneous whole-body plethysmography plus EEG/EMG arousal-state scoring, backed by ex vivo nucleus tractus solitarius (nTS) slice electrophysiology from the same genotype.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the specific lesion this hypothesis targets: MeCP2 loss produces synaptic hyperexcitability in nTS respiratory cell groups that is reversed by BDNF in slices and by systemically dosed TrkB agonist in vivo with acute reversal of spontaneous apnoeas (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 25147297); respiratory abnormalities including altered respiratory frequency are present and pharmacologically improvable in heterozygous females (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 22302819).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes — nTS relay neurons and ventral respiratory column rhythmogenic neurons are the cells assayed, in the mosaic X-inactivation genotype that matches affected girls (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 40673967 for Mecp2+/- as closest analogue).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Apnoea frequency/duration and respiratory irregularity by plethysmography, resolved by arousal state (wake-active, quiet wake, NREM, REM); nTS evoked/spontaneous excitatory synaptic drive as the target-engagement readout.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Mouse apnoea counts already produced a positive preclinical signal for a mechanism (5-HT1A/D2) that failed in humans (EVIDENCE, contradictory, NCT02790034), so the model has a documented false-positive history; apnoea in mutants is partly arousal-state dependent, so unstratified counts can reflect activity rather than rhythmogenesis (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID 25147297); mice cannot model paediatric tolerability ceilings or the seizure/cardiovascular liabilities that limit human dosing; behavioural improvement in Mecp2+/- mice can occur without circuit normalisation, a general warning that rodent endpoints overstate benefit (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID 40673967).

plan.critical_question: Is the brainstem apnoea endpoint itself measurable with enough state-resolved signal-to-noise to detect a true drug effect — and does any candidate agent produce verified nTS target engagement at a dose that reduces apnoea within an arousal state? I.e. discriminate sarizotan's three failure explanations (wrong node vs. no engagement vs. endpoint failure) before any new molecule is advanced.
plan.proposed_experiment: A single endpoint-qualification-plus-engagement study in symptomatic Mecp2+/- females (n sized for within-animal crossover), run in two linked arms. Arm A (endpoint qualification, drug-free): 3 repeated plethysmography + EEG/EMG sessions per animal, 7 days apart, to compute within-animal test-retest variance of apnoea rate overall versus apnoea rate within each arousal state, and the detectable effect size for each. Arm B (engagement-anchored pharmacology, crossover against vehicle): LM22A-4 (TrkB partial agonist, the only agent with demonstrated nTS engagement in Mecp2 tissue, PMID 25147297, PMID 22302819) and fenfluramine (the agent now in Phase 3, NCT07503444), each dosed to a pre-declared plasma/brain exposure, with sarizotan included as a built-in benchmark of the human-negative node (NCT02790034). Terminal readout in the same animals: nTS slice recordings of excitatory synaptic drive ± ex vivo drug, so every behavioural result is paired with an independent measure of whether the brainstem target was actually engaged. Pre-register the state-stratified apnoea rate as primary and total apnoea count as secondary.
plan.model: Symptomatic Mecp2+/- female mice with paired in vivo plethysmography/EEG-EMG and terminal nTS slice electrophysiology; Mecp2-/y males as a high-severity mechanistic comparator.
plan.primary_readout: Primary: apnoea rate within matched arousal state (drug vs. vehicle, within animal). Co-primary: nTS excitatory synaptic drive normalised toward wild-type as target engagement. Secondary: total unstratified apnoea count (to quantify how much signal the conventional endpoint loses).
plan.supportive_result: State-stratified apnoea rate has materially lower variance than total count and detects a reduction for LM22A-4 that is accompanied by normalised nTS synaptic drive, while sarizotan shows little or no nTS engagement at tolerated exposure. This would mean sarizotan failed for node/engagement reasons and that an engagement-anchored, state-resolved endpoint exists — justifying a TrkB-branch (or fenfluramine) programme with a target-engagement-defined dose and a state-resolved human endpoint (polysomnography-scored, not averaged daytime apnoea counts).
plan.negative_result: Either (a) within-animal test-retest variance of apnoea rate remains high even after state stratification, so no feasible trial could detect a plausible effect — endpoint failure dominates; or (b) an agent normalises nTS synaptic drive yet apnoea rate within arousal state is unchanged, meaning corrected nTS excitability does not control the breathing phenotype; or (c) apnoea reduction tracks only with changes in arousal/activity, not with nTS engagement — confirming the arousal confound (INFERENCE, PMID 25147297).
plan.decision_enabled: Go/no-go on investing in brainstem small-molecule pharmacology at all, and if go, on which branch. Supportive → advance the engagement-validated branch (TrkB-directed, or fenfluramine with a declared engagement surrogate) and fund human polysomnography endpoint development first. Negative via (a) → do not run another respiratory-endpoint trial; spend on endpoint/biomarker development (state-resolved home polysomnography, autonomic indices) before any molecule. Negative via (b) or (c) → deprioritise brainstem E/I stabilisation as a standalone strategy and reallocate to mechanism-agnostic MeCP2-function restoration or convergent neurotrophic nodes (PMID 35460749, PMID 37633263), accepting that respiratory morbidity may only improve as a consequence of broader correction (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
